blocks.prompt: 3 (i) Use the factor theorem to determine if the first polynomial is a factor of the second polynomial: \(x + 1\), \(x^{2} - 1\).
blocks.explanation:
Yeh haan ya nahi wala sawal hai: kya \(x + 1\), \(x^{2} - 1\) ka factor hai?
Factor ka matlab: woh cheez jo poora poora divide kare aur kuch na bache, jaise 3 number 12 ka factor hai kyunke 12 ko 3 se divide karne par remainder 0 hai.
Factor theorem kehta hai: \(x - a\) factor hai sirf tab jab \(f(a) = 0\) ho.
Plan: \(a\) pehchanna, \(f(a)\) nikalna, faisla karna, aur synthetic division se tasdeeq karna.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(f(x) = x^{2} - 1\), mumkin factor \(x + 1\).
Humein find karna hai: \(x + 1\) factor hai ya nahi.
Tareeqa: Factor theorem: \(x - a\), \(f(x)\) ka factor hai agar aur sirf agar \(f(a) = 0\). Yeh remainder theorem hi ki ek shakal hai: \(f(a)\) remainder hota hai, aur factor wahi hai jo zero remainder chhore.

Divisor ko \(x - a\) ki shakal mein likhein
\[x + 1 = x - (-1)\]
\[a = -1\]
Kyun: Theorem divisor \(x - a\) ke liye hai, yani beech mein minus ka sign chahiye. \(x + 1\) mein plus hai, to hum likhte hain \(x - (-1)\); is tarah \(a = -1\) negative aata hai. Asaan tareeqa: divisor ko zero ke barabar rakh dein, \(x + 1 = 0\) se \(x = -1\); yahi value rakhni hai.
Dhyan dein: \(x + 1\) dekh kar \(a = 1\) le lena sab se aam ghalti hai.

\(f(-1)\) nikalein
\[f(-1) = (-1)^{2} - 1\]
\[= 1 - 1\]
\[= 0\]
Kyun: Negative number ki even power (2, 4) positive aati hai, aur odd power (1, 3) negative rehti hai; jaise \((-2)^2 = 4\) lekin \((-2)^3 = -8\). Pehle har power alag se nikalein, phir coefficient se multiply karein, aur aakhir mein jama karein.

Faisla karein
\[f(-1) = 0\]
Is liye \(x + 1\), \(x^{2} - 1\) ka factor hai.
Kyun: \(f(-1)\) remainder hai, aur remainder zero ka matlab hai ke division poori poori hui, kuch nahi bacha. Factor theorem yahi kehta hai: \(f(a) = 0\) hai to \(x - a\) factor hai.

Tasdeeq: synthetic division se
\[\begin{array}{r|rrr} -1 & 1 & 0 & -1 \\  &  & -1 & 1 \\ \hline & 1 & -1 & \boxed{0} \end{array}\]
\[x^{2} - 1 = (x + 1)(x - 1)\]
Kyun: Box wala aakhri number remainder hai aur woh 0 hai, is liye division poori hui. Baqi neeche wale numbers quotient ke coefficients hain, aur quotient ki degree polynomial se ek kam hoti hai, is liye quotient \(x - 1\) bana. Yani polynomial ko \(x + 1\) aur \(x - 1\) ke product ki shakal mein likh sakte hain; yahi factor hone ka matlab hai.

blocks.prompt: 3 (ii) Use the factor theorem to determine if the first polynomial is a factor of the second polynomial: \(x - 2\), \(x^{2} - 5x + 6\).
blocks.explanation:
Yeh haan ya nahi wala sawal hai: kya \(x - 2\), \(x^{2} - 5x + 6\) ka factor hai?
Factor ka matlab: woh cheez jo poora poora divide kare aur kuch na bache, jaise 3 number 12 ka factor hai kyunke 12 ko 3 se divide karne par remainder 0 hai.
Factor theorem kehta hai: \(x - a\) factor hai sirf tab jab \(f(a) = 0\) ho.
Plan: \(a\) pehchanna, \(f(a)\) nikalna, faisla karna, aur synthetic division se tasdeeq karna.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(f(x) = x^{2} - 5x + 6\), mumkin factor \(x - 2\).
Humein find karna hai: \(x - 2\) factor hai ya nahi.
Tareeqa: Factor theorem: \(x - a\), \(f(x)\) ka factor hai agar aur sirf agar \(f(a) = 0\). Yeh remainder theorem hi ki ek shakal hai: \(f(a)\) remainder hota hai, aur factor wahi hai jo zero remainder chhore.

Divisor ko \(x - a\) ki shakal mein dekhein
\[x - 2 = x - a\]
\[a = 2\]
Kyun: Remainder theorem aur factor theorem dono divisor \(x - a\) ke liye bayan kiye gaye hain. Yahan divisor mein minus ka sign pehle se mojood hai, is liye \(a\) seedha \(2\) hai. Yaani hum \(x\) ki jagah woh value rakhenge jis par divisor zero ho jata hai.

\(f(2)\) nikalein
\[f(2) = (2)^{2} - 5(2) + 6\]
\[= 4 - 10 + 6\]
\[= 0\]
Kyun: Pehle har power ki value nikalein, phir us ko coefficient se multiply karein, aur aakhir mein sab terms jama karein. Ek waqt mein ek kaam karne se hisaab ki ghalti nahi hoti.

Faisla karein
\[f(2) = 0\]
Is liye \(x - 2\), \(x^{2} - 5x + 6\) ka factor hai.
Kyun: \(f(2)\) remainder hai, aur remainder zero ka matlab hai ke division poori poori hui, kuch nahi bacha. Factor theorem yahi kehta hai: \(f(a) = 0\) hai to \(x - a\) factor hai.

Tasdeeq: synthetic division se
\[\begin{array}{r|rrr} 2 & 1 & -5 & 6 \\  &  & 2 & -6 \\ \hline & 1 & -3 & \boxed{0} \end{array}\]
\[x^{2} - 5x + 6 = (x - 2)(x - 3)\]
Kyun: Box wala aakhri number remainder hai aur woh 0 hai, is liye division poori hui. Baqi neeche wale numbers quotient ke coefficients hain, aur quotient ki degree polynomial se ek kam hoti hai, is liye quotient \(x - 3\) bana. Yani polynomial ko \(x - 2\) aur \(x - 3\) ke product ki shakal mein likh sakte hain; yahi factor hone ka matlab hai.

blocks.prompt: 3 (iii) Use the factor theorem to determine if the first polynomial is a factor of the second polynomial: \(x + 1\), \(x^{3} + x^{2} + x - 3\).
blocks.explanation:
Yeh haan ya nahi wala sawal hai: kya \(x + 1\), \(x^{3} + x^{2} + x - 3\) ka factor hai?
Factor ka matlab: woh cheez jo poora poora divide kare aur kuch na bache, jaise 3 number 12 ka factor hai kyunke 12 ko 3 se divide karne par remainder 0 hai.
Factor theorem kehta hai: \(x - a\) factor hai sirf tab jab \(f(a) = 0\) ho.
Plan: \(a\) pehchanna, \(f(a)\) nikalna, faisla karna, aur synthetic division se tasdeeq karna.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(f(x) = x^{3} + x^{2} + x - 3\), mumkin factor \(x + 1\).
Humein find karna hai: \(x + 1\) factor hai ya nahi.
Tareeqa: Factor theorem: \(x - a\), \(f(x)\) ka factor hai agar aur sirf agar \(f(a) = 0\). Yeh remainder theorem hi ki ek shakal hai: \(f(a)\) remainder hota hai, aur factor wahi hai jo zero remainder chhore.

Divisor ko \(x - a\) ki shakal mein likhein
\[x + 1 = x - (-1)\]
\[a = -1\]
Kyun: Theorem divisor \(x - a\) ke liye hai, yani beech mein minus ka sign chahiye. \(x + 1\) mein plus hai, to hum likhte hain \(x - (-1)\); is tarah \(a = -1\) negative aata hai. Asaan tareeqa: divisor ko zero ke barabar rakh dein, \(x + 1 = 0\) se \(x = -1\); yahi value rakhni hai.
Dhyan dein: \(x + 1\) dekh kar \(a = 1\) le lena sab se aam ghalti hai.

\(f(-1)\) nikalein
\[f(-1) = (-1)^{3} + (-1)^{2} + (-1) - 3\]
\[= -1 + 1 - 1 - 3\]
\[= -4\]
Kyun: Negative number ki even power (2, 4) positive aati hai, aur odd power (1, 3) negative rehti hai; jaise \((-2)^2 = 4\) lekin \((-2)^3 = -8\). Pehle har power alag se nikalein, phir coefficient se multiply karein, aur aakhir mein jama karein.

Faisla karein
\[f(-1) = -4 \ne 0\]
Is liye \(x + 1\), \(x^{3} + x^{2} + x - 3\) ka factor nahi hai.
Kyun: Factor theorem ke mutabiq factor hone ke liye \(f(-1)\) ka zero hona zaroori hai. Yahan \(-4\) bachta hai, yani division poori nahi hoti, jaise 13 ko 3 se divide karein to 1 bach jata hai aur 3 is liye 13 ka factor nahi.

Tasdeeq: synthetic division se
\[\begin{array}{r|rrrr} -1 & 1 & 1 & 1 & -3 \\  &  & -1 & 0 & -1 \\ \hline & 1 & 0 & 1 & \boxed{-4} \end{array}\]
Kyun: Synthetic division ka aakhri (box wala) number remainder hai. Woh \(-4\) hai, zero nahi, aur yeh bilkul \(f(-1)\) ke barabar hai. Do tareeqon se ek hi nateeja aaya: \(x + 1\) factor nahi hai.
blocks.final_answer: Nahi, \(x + 1\), \(x^{3} + x^{2} + x - 3\) ka factor nahi hai (remainder \(-4\)).
